title: Move a lamp's plug from a scorched socket to the sound one
instruction: The left socket is scorched - move the lamp's plug to the sound socket beside it.
context: A scorched receptacle faceplate marks a burned contact that can arc and start a fire; the appliance is moved to a sound socket on the same circuit and the damaged one is taken out of service. Scorched faceplates are a standard electrical-inspection finding.
setup: All parts are rigid boxes on a flat table (the station scene). Two adjacent receptacle pedestals, each 12x8x17 cm, stand side by side duplex-style - edges touching, centres 12 cm apart - at (30, -6) cm and (18, -6) cm: the farther one blackened brown (scorched socket), the nearer one light grey (sound socket). Each socket's well is formed by two dark-grey guide walls 1x6x1.2 cm standing on the pedestal top, their inner faces 8 cm apart. A lamp plug 4x3.5x3.5 cm, 40 g, dark grey, is seated in the scorched socket's well, resting on the well floor.
scoring: 1.0 when the plug rests in the sound (right) socket's well: its centre within 1.2 cm of that well's centre in both x and y and at the seat height within 8 mm. Anything else - the plug left in the scorched socket, lying on the table, or knocked off - is 0. Do-nothing: 0.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed; the scene reset reseats the plug in the scorched socket.
fidelity: A rigid-body stand-in of moving a plug to a sound receptacle. Each socket is a 17 cm pedestal with two guide walls forming an 8 cm-wide well; the plug is a 4 cm grip stand-in (its cord and prongs are not modeled). The damage is marked by the blackened pedestal a camera can see, matching how a scorched receptacle is actually spotted during inspection.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (hit the step limit); demo: 1.0
